newsitem.title: USA: Avigen tumor therapy effective in tests.
newsitem.headline: Avigen tumor therapy effective in tests.

text.p: Avigen Inc said pre-clinical tests showed its adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector system was effective in shrinking human brain tumors implanted into mice.
Company researchers conducted the study in collaboration with Nagoya University in Japan. Their results are published in the November 6 issue of Gene Therapy.

The AAV vector system is a means of delivering a gene that kills tumor cells. The gene is delivered through a virus that exists in nature and attaches to tumors. The virus used, the AAV vector, is harmless to humans.

The company said the study just completed was one in a series of pre-clinical tests it would conduct before beginning official clinical studes aimed at obtaining the approval of the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration. It said it expected to begin clinical studies in late 1997.
